title: First-run warmup flow — PRD journal
content:
Context / motivation:
- New customers (and devs iterating locally) hit poor first impressions due to:
  * cold model/gpu scheduling delays (esp on Dedicated)
  * high latency on first session interactions -> perceived product slowness
  * early token cost for users trying things out (they churn before real usage)
- Goal: make the first 5–30s of a developer or user journey feel instant and useful, while not disproportionately increasing infra cost.

High-level proposal (warmup flow):
- On first session (or explicitly opt-in demo runner) run a lightweight preflight that:
  1) sends a tiny context vector to the runtime to ensure model is loaded / kernel warmed
  2) primes a short interactive demo prompt tailored to the user persona (dev, product manager, integrator)
  3) optionally prefetch embeddings or small KV snippets for common starter intents
- Two modes: "frictionless" (auto warmup for logged-in orgs) vs "manual demo" (explicit button for anonymous/guest users).
- Provide telemetry and a short UX funnel so we can measure perceived improvement vs infra cost.

User stories (rough):
- As a developer trying the API, I want my first simple request to return quickly so I can iterate, so that I don't leave the sign-up flow.
- As a product tester, I want a guided short demo to show possible outputs without writing prompts, so I can evaluate the model faster.
- As an admin on Dedicated, I want warmup to respect capacity/quotas and not create noisy load during busy windows.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Warmup trigger executes in < 1s on the client side and completes model-ready check within 10s on average for Hosted.
- 20% reduction in median time-to-first-token for new sessions in the A/B cohort.
- Config toggles exist in Console: enable_auto_warmup (org-level), demo_mode (project-level).
- No SLO violations introduced by warmup traffic during peak hours (sre gating).

Implementation sketch (tech notes):
- Server: add orchestrated warmup endpoint /v1/warmup that performs a light inference pass (short sequence, deterministic) and returns a small readiness token + latency telemetry.
- Runtime: lightweight warmup should prefer a cheap model variant (quantized or distilled) if configured, with fallback to full model.
- Routing: warmup requests tagged and routed to low-priority warmup pool to avoid interfering with customer traffic.
- Client: SDK helper warmup.enableFirstRunWarmup() that peeks and stores readiness TTL in client cache (localStorage / session cookie) to avoid repeating often.

Cost & constraints:
- Warmup traffic increases token throughput; need estimate: assume X warmups/day = N tokens/day. For Hosted freemium this is acceptable; for Dedicated, respect org quotas and provide rate-limits.
- Potential extra GPU spin-ups -> avoid if org has strict cost caps, provide opt-out.
- Privacy: warmup payloads must not persist customer prompt content in analytics unless consented. Use hashed telemetry.

Metrics to track (experiment):
- time_to_first_token (new session) — primary metric
- onboarding_conversion_7d (did warmup improve trial->paid)
- warmup_cost_tokens_per_user and warmup_gpu_spikes (infra impact)
- perceived_latency_survey (optional micro UX survey after first run)

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Warmup noise could mask real SLO issues if we route incorrectly. Need dedicated observability and tagging.
- Users may abuse warmup to keep models hot -> implement fair-use throttles.
- Using distilled variants could produce mismatched outputs vs production model; must label demo outputs clearly.

Experiment plan (A/B):
- Cohort A: no warmup (control).
- Cohort B: frictionless warmup for first session only.
- Duration: 4 weeks or until 10k new sessions collected.
- Stop conditions: any spike in 99th percentile latency or increase in error rate > 3x baseline.

UX / demo copy (working):
- Inline tooltip: "Speed up your first request — try a guided example"
- Demo sequence: 3 micro-prompts, each < 40 tokens, covering: "summarize", "rewrite", "extract" for developer persona.
- Visual: small progress shimmer and a subtle badge "instant preview" so users know output is a demo.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How long should client cache TTL be? 15 minutes vs 2 hours? (Mika prefers 10m for public pages).
- Should warmup count against free-tier quotas? (billing/legal consult)
- Dedicated: provide org-level opt-in with safety nets (max warmups/hr).
- Perf verification: run bench on staging with representative models and 3 sequence lengths.

Quick prototype steps (what I'll build next):
- Small local PoC: implement /v1/warmup in dev cluster + SDK stub (2 days)
- Add Console toggle and minimal telemetry tagging (1 week)
- Run internal dogfood across 5 teams -> gather qualitative feedback (2 weeks)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep warmup prompt generic and non-sensitive. Use templated persona snippets.
- Ping @noah on Slack for SRE gating + throttling heuristics (see thread: slack.redwood/threads/C0912-warmup-heuristics).
- Add JIRA ticket RED-4287 to track Dedicated opt-in work.

Links and references:
- internal bench: https://bench.redwood-internal/reports/warmup-2026-02
- related idea: session-presets-personalization (overlap on demo prompts)

End notes: warmup seems low-friction feature that can improve first impressions and trial conversion if we contain cost and surface attribution clearly. Next: validate with small internal cohort, iterate on TTL/variant selection, and write clearer UX copy for Console.
